app/src/api.ts:112-127 — plain fetch() with a Map cache; no AbortSignal, streams, or newer fetch options
app/package.json:14 — typescript ^7.0.2, the Go-native compiler, stable only since 2026-07-08 (~3.5 months old)

reach.rationale: Runtime code uses exclusively long-stable platform APIs (History, fetch, URL, Map/Set, replaceChildren, scrollIntoView) and Node built-ins. The single recent thing is the toolchain: TypeScript 7.0, stable ~3.5 months, used in the central build pipeline — that sits between anchor 1 (only long-stable) and anchor 3 (a recently-stable API in a central place).

evidence: app/package.json:10 — TypeScript appears only as 'tsc --noEmit' in the build script; one line to swap or remove
app/server.mjs:1-6 — dependency-free production server using only node:http/fs/path/url
app/tsconfig.json — vanilla config (target ES2022, moduleResolution bundler), no experimental compiler options
containment.rationale: Nothing to contain: the only recent tool (TS 7) is confined to package.json and the build script, swappable in one line, and there is no vite.config or any flag at all. The shipped runtime has zero recent-API exposure.

evidence: app/package.json:10 — 'tsc --noEmit' in build buys 8-12x faster type-checks (TS 7 native compiler) for free
app/package.json:14-15 — both deps are the current stable majors the ecosystem itself defaults to (create-vite shipped TS 7 in Oct 2026)
app/src/dom.ts:1-36 — hand-rolled h()/append helpers instead of reaching for any newer rendering API
justification.rationale: Every use is justified and none is gratuitous: Vite 8 and TS 7 are the current stable releases with concrete speed benefits, used exactly per ecosystem defaults, with no novelty-driven runtime APIs, flags, or previews.

findings.issue: typescript ^7.0.2 is the newly-Go-native compiler, stable only since 2026-07-08; its programmatic API was reported as not stable before 7.1.
findings.suggestion: Fine as used (CLI-only 'tsc --noEmit'), but keep an eye on 7.x patch releases and avoid adopting the programmatic API until it stabilizes.

summary: This app reaches for essentially zero experimental APIs: the entire runtime is built on platform APIs that have been stable for years (History, fetch, DOM core, flexbox/custom properties), and the Node production server uses only long-stable built-ins. The only recent choices are toolchain-level — TypeScript 7 (stable July 2026) and Vite 8 (stable March 2026) — both current stable majors used exactly as the ecosystem defaults, with no experimental flags or config anywhere. Risk of breaking-change exposure is negligible.
